info.description:
Authentication

API key must be provided in the X-API-Key header:
X-API-Key: {your-api-key-guid}

Note: V2 does not support query parameter authentication for security reasons. If header-based authentication presents integration challenges for your use case, please contact our support team to discuss alternative solutions.

Naming

'Clientspaces' in this API are called 'Subaccounts' in the web app. The API keeps the original resource name (/api/v2/clientspaces) for backward compatibility; they are the same thing.

Rate Limits

Limits are per organization (not per endpoint). The main account and its workspaces share one bucket; each clientspace (called a Subaccount in the web app) has its own bucket.
Standard: 60 requests per minute (all orgs by default).
Elevated tier: 300 requests per minute for the main account and its workspaces (Business, Agency including trial, and UltraMode addon).
Clientspaces (Subaccounts): 60 requests per minute each, independent of the main account and of other clientspaces.
Exceeding the limit returns HTTP 429 with Retry-After (seconds to wait) plus X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, and X-RateLimit-Reset (seconds remaining in the window, suffixed with s). Wait for Retry-After before retrying; do not retry immediately. A quiet 60-second window clears the counter.
Automation (N8N, MCP, Zapier): a single workflow step often issues several HTTP calls (list messages, resolve sender, send reply). Count those API calls against the per-account limit, not the number of workflow runs.

Done-for-you provider integration

Flow: create sessions with POST /api/v2/oauth/sessions/bulk (one per mailbox), open each authUrl as that mailbox, and poll GET /api/v2/oauth/sessions?batchId=... every 15 to 30 seconds.
Google Workspace: before the first sign-in, the Workspace admin trusts our client in Admin console > Security > API controls > App access control > Configure new app: search for client ID 23688329945-8lisrrrsg5q22b3kiikm27n792nf9qkc.apps.googleusercontent.com (also returned as clientId on each session), scope it to all users and mark it Trusted (guide). If the app is not trusted, Google shows "Access blocked" and never returns to us, so the session stays Pending until it expires.
Microsoft 365: each mailbox needs Authenticated SMTP and IMAP enabled (Microsoft 365 admin center > Active users > Mail > Manage email apps, guide). The tenant must allow user consent for our app (client ID 56fe48ec-6d11-4c16-8471-353196c3f401), or a Global Administrator grants tenant-wide consent once; until then, sign-in shows "Need admin approval".
authUrl is a single-use link bound to the session email; do not publish it.

Changelog

2.25.0 (2026-11-18): Campaigns: companySendLimit caps how many new prospects at one recipient company (email domain) are emailed per UTC day; null uses the workspace setting (send null in PATCH /api/v2/campaigns/{id} to reset a campaign to it), 0 turns it off, 1-100 sets the campaign's own limit (other values return 422). Follow-ups are never held back and free email providers are not limited.
New GET/PATCH /api/v2/account/settings: companySendLimit sets the default for the workspace the key belongs to; 0 turns it off (0-100, other values return 422).
2.24.1 (2026-11-17): Orders: a reused domain that was cancelled but is still inside its paid registration year is accepted again; its yearly renewal resumes at the expiry date.
2.24.0 (2026-11-17): Senders connected with OAuth through API v2 now start with customWarmupTag null (no warmup body tag) instead of a default derived from the organization; set it with PATCH /api/v2/senders/{id} if you filter warmup mail by it. Senders created earlier keep their tag. The messageId of sent messages from keepwarm campaigns is now the Message-ID the email was actually sent with.
2.23.0 (2026-11-17): Senders gain paused on every sender response, and PATCH /api/v2/senders/{id} accepts paused to pause (true) or resume (false) sending. A paused sender sends no campaign or warmup emails, even with warmup: true. PATCH /api/v2/senders/{id} now succeeds reliably while the sender is being updated concurrently.
2.22.1 (2026-11-16): Sessions add clientId, the OAuth client ID their authUrl uses (on create, bulk, GET and list), so a Google Workspace admin knows which app to trust.
2.22.0 (2026-11-16): Connect Google and Microsoft mailboxes with OAuth. POST /api/v2/senders/connect connects a Google mailbox from a refresh token you hold (or restores a deleted sender with the same id) and POST /api/v2/senders/{id}/reconnect replaces the tokens of a Google sender; the token must belong to the sender's email (422 otherwise), and the sender limit applies to connect (403 when an upgrade raises it, 422 otherwise) but not to reconnect.
Hosted OAuth sessions, for mailboxes you cannot get tokens for: POST /api/v2/oauth/sessions (one mailbox) and POST /api/v2/oauth/sessions/bulk (1 to 200) return a single-use authUrl per mailbox; sign in as that mailbox and it is connected as a sender, or an existing OAuth sender with that email gets new tokens (mode: Reconnect). status is Pending, Connected (with senderId), Failed (with error) or Expired; a sign-in with the wrong mailbox keeps the session Pending with error set. In bulk, mailboxes that cannot be connected (managed, already a sender, over the sender limit) get a Failed session without authUrl. Poll GET /api/v2/oauth/sessions/{id} about every 5 seconds, or GET /api/v2/oauth/sessions?batchId=... every 15 to 30 seconds; authUrl is only returned when the session is created.
Your own Google OAuth apps: GET and POST /api/v2/oauth/Google/apps, GET, PATCH and DELETE /api/v2/oauth/Google/apps/{id}. Pass the app id as oauthAppId on connect, reconnect and sessions. Creating an app or using oauthAppId needs an active plan, UltraMode or Clientspace subscription (403 PLAN_REQUIRED); the secret is never returned, and DELETE returns 409 while an active sender uses the app. For sessions, add https://app.manyreach.com/e/auth/googlecallback as a redirect URI of your client. Microsoft apps are not available yet (the Microsoft list is empty).
Sender responses add oauthAppId, platformOAuthAppUsed and managed. On connect and sessions, the 409 for a mailbox that is already a sender in this account includes its senderId. Existing endpoints are unchanged.
2.21.0 (2026-11-13): Campaign prospect sendingStatus can be SenderMoved: the prospect's follow-ups stopped because its sender was moved to another workspace; moving the sender back restores the previous status. Existing statuses are unchanged.
2.20.0 (2026-11-13): Move a sender to another workspace. POST /api/v2/senders/{id}/move with workspaceId moves the sender to the main account or one of its workspaces or clientspaces and returns the moved sender. Call it with the main account API key; it can move senders that are in the main account or any of its workspaces and clientspaces (other keys: 403 MAIN_ACCOUNT_REQUIRED). A sender or workspace outside the account returns 404; moving a sender to the workspace it is already in returns 422, as does a retry after a successful move. The destination's sender limit applies as for POST /api/v2/senders. Only the sender moves: its campaigns, prospects and tags stay in the old workspace, and follow-ups of those campaigns no longer send from it. Existing endpoints are unchanged.
2.19.0 (2026-11-12): Lead search with Data Tokens: new /api/v2/lead-search endpoints, described for AI agents (MCP). GET /api/v2/lead-search/filters lists the allowed values of the lookup filters (countries, regions, industries, employee and revenue ranges) and names the free-text filters; GET /api/v2/lead-search/services?q= suggests services. POST /api/v2/lead-search/preview returns the match count and the first 50 people (no emails) for flat include / exclude filters (jobTitles, excludeJobTitles, countries, ...) plus optional companyDomains / excludeCompanyDomains (up to 10,000 each) and maxPerCompany; previews never use Data Tokens (1,000 per account per UTC day, then 429 with Retry-After).
POST /api/v2/lead-search/searches finds up to target new verified emails (1 to 5,000; above 5,000 returns 400) and adds them as prospects to a list (listId, or a new list listName), optionally a campaign (campaignId) and a tag; it returns 202 with batchId and maxTokens. POST /api/v2/lead-search/find-emails finds emails for 1 to 5,000 people you provide (linkedinUrl, or firstName, lastName and companyWebsite / companyDomain, with your own ref) and returns accepted and rejected. Both charge 10 Data Tokens per new verified email added, need 10 Data Tokens per wanted email to start (402 INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS), and run one batch per account at a time (429).
GET /api/v2/lead-search/batches/{batchId} returns status, progress, counts, tokensCharged, prospectIds and, for find-emails, per-person results; POST /api/v2/lead-search/batches/{batchId}/cancel stops a batch. GET, POST and DELETE /api/v2/lead-search/saved-searches list, create and delete saved searches. Request bodies above 2 MB return 413; lists, campaigns, batches and saved searches of other accounts return 404. GET /api/v2/account/data-tokens: emailFinder now has status live and unit verified email added. Existing endpoints are unchanged.
2.18.0 (2026-11-09): POST /api/v2/orders/{id}/checkout returns 422 when a Domain item is already registered, so it can't be bought. The error message names the domains. Add a domain you already own as an ExistingDomain item instead.
2.17.0 (2026-11-03): Date and cursor query parameters ending in Z (UTC) are read as UTC: dateStart and dateEnd on GET /api/v2/campaigns/{id}/stats, and startingAfter on GET /api/v2/messages, GET /api/v2/orders and GET /api/v2/prospects/{id}/messages. Previously they were shifted by the server time zone, so a day range could start on the previous day and a nextCursor passed back as startingAfter could skip or repeat items.
2.16.0 (2026-11-02): Sender campaign stats. GET /api/v2/senders/campaign-stats lists, for every sender, the campaign emails sent (sent, first emails initialSent) and the hardBounced, softBounced, opened, clicked and replied counts they received, with bounceRate (hardBounced / initialSent, one decimal), summed over the UTC days dateStart to dateEnd (default the last 14 days; history is kept for 90 days), up to 100 senders per page. GET /api/v2/senders/{id}/campaign-stats returns the same totals for one sender plus one entry per UTC day in days, and GET /api/v2/senders/domains/campaign-stats returns them per sending domain with the number of senders. Campaign emails only (warmup excluded), counted by the UTC day each email was sent, refreshed about hourly; counts settle within 30 days of the send day. opened, clicked and replied count emails with at least one such event; replies exclude auto-replies. hardBounced and softBounced count prospects whose first email from the sender bounced permanently, or got a temporary delivery failure (not suppressed; a hard bounce after 3 occurrences); soft bounces before 2026-09-03 are counted as hard. Existing sender responses are unchanged.
GET /api/v2/senders/warmup-stats responds faster for large pages. A page past the last one returns an empty items list; pagination.totalItems is the number of senders.
2.15.1 (2026-10-30): POST /api/v2/senders fills warmup settings you leave out or send as 0 with the app's defaults: warmupDailyLimit 5 and warmupReplyPercent 30. When warmupDailyLimit is also left out (or 0) and warmupDailyLimitIncrease, warmupDailyLimitIncreasePercent and warmupDailyLimitIncreaseToMax are all left out (or false/0), the warmup limit ramps up by 5% a day to 30, as for senders added in the app. Senders created with warmup: true and no warmup settings now start warming up instead of sending no warmup emails. Non-zero values you send are kept, and a warmup limit you set without ramp settings stays fixed.
2.15.0 (2026-10-24): Sender test emails. POST /api/v2/senders/{id}/test-emails sends a test email from the sender to up to 10 addresses (to), with your own subject and body, for example for an inbox placement test. Each address gets its own email. Optional plainText, trackOpens and trackClicks (default off). Placeholders such as {{SENDER_FIRSTNAME}} and spintax are processed as in the app's test emails. The response lists each address with status (Sent, Failed, Blocked for addresses on your blocklist, Skipped when not attempted) and, for sent emails, messageId and sentAt, plus how many test emails the sender and the account can still send today (senderRemainingToday, accountRemainingToday). Test emails are limited to 50 per sender and 500 per account per UTC day, shared with test emails sent from the app; above that the call returns 429 with Retry-After, as does a second call for the same sender while one is running. Each address the email is sent to uses one sending credit (creditsUsed); if the account doesn't have enough sending credits for every address, the call returns 402 INSUFFICIENT_SENDING_CREDITS and nothing is sent. A disconnected sender returns the new error 409 SENDER_DISCONNECTED; 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE means test emails are temporarily unavailable and the call is safe to retry. Existing endpoints are unchanged.
2.14.0 (2026-10-22): Sender warmup stats. GET /api/v2/senders/{id}/warmup-stats returns the sender's Warmup Score (the same 0-100 value as on the Senders page: the share of warmup emails sent in the last 14 days that were not found in spam; null when nothing was sent) with warmup emails sent, notSpam (not found in spam, including emails not checked yet) and spam for the last 14 days, and per UTC day in days for dateStart to dateEnd (default the last 14 days; warmup history is kept for 30 days). GET /api/v2/senders/warmup-stats lists the score and 14-day totals of all senders, up to 100 per page. Unlike the page, the score is also returned while warmup is off. The score measures placement in the warmup network, not the inbox rate of campaign emails. Existing sender responses are unchanged.
Order item DNS and forwarding. GET /api/v2/orders/{id}/items/{itemId}/dns-records lists the DNS records of a domain item on a completed order, each with managed set for records Manyreach maintains for your mailboxes and forwarding. POST .../dns-records adds a TXT, CNAME, A or AAAA record (not on managed names such as SPF at @, _dmarc, www or the mailbox DKIM selectors: 422; the same record again: 409 DUPLICATE_RESOURCE) and DELETE .../dns-records/{recordId} removes one you added; managed records can't be changed or deleted (422). GET and PATCH .../forwarding read and change where the domain redirects visitors; when a change covers every domain of the order (the order has only that domain), the order's forwardingDomain is updated too. Changes are confirmed with the DNS provider before the call returns; if the provider doesn't confirm, the call returns the new error 502 PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE and can be retried. Existing order and order item responses are unchanged.
2.13.0 (2026-10-20): Four new outbound webhook events, available on the API & Integrations page. Payloads of existing events are unchanged.
prospect_unsubscribed: the first time a prospect unsubscribes (unsubscribe link or header, AI, a status you set in Unibox or by reply, or the API; not bulk status changes or CRM edits). The prospect event payload plus unsubSource when known (for example link, api, manualreply, manualstatus, aisentiment).
prospect_not_interested: when a prospect's status changes to Not interested (AI, or set by you in Unibox or the API; not bulk changes). The same payload as prospect_interested, with replyId, toEmail and receivingSenderId when the status came from a reply.
prospect_bounced: a hard or soft bounce of a campaign email, detected automatically (warmup excluded). The prospect event payload plus bounceStatus (hard or soft) and statusDesc (the bounce reason), each only when known.
sender_disconnected: one of your senders was disconnected automatically (sign-in or sending errors; not when you disconnect it yourself). Its own payload: eventId, senderId, senderEmail, reason and disconnectedAt (UTC, ISO 8601).
2.12.0 (2026-10-19): replyToEmail on POST /api/v2/campaigns, PATCH /api/v2/campaigns/{id} and campaign responses is deprecated: it is still accepted but no longer applied, and responses return null. Replies go to the sending mailbox; to route replies elsewhere set Reply-To per sender with PATCH /api/v2/senders/{id} (replyTo).
2.11.1 (2026-10-18): PATCH /api/v2/clientspaces/{id} with separateCredits: false moves the clientspace's remaining credit balance back to the agency before switching it to shared credits, so no credits are left unusable. If the move fails, the request returns 500 and nothing is changed.
2.11.0 (2026-10-16): GET /api/v2/senders accepts status=blacklisted: only senders whose email domain is currently listed by the daily blacklist scan (same as the Blacklisted badge in the app). Requires Blacklist Monitoring; without it the list is empty.
2.10.5 (2026-10-14): Campaigns created with POST /api/v2/campaigns or updated with PATCH /api/v2/campaigns/{id} with scheduleSendOnDateEnabled start at scheduleSendOnDate plus scheduleSendOnDateHours:scheduleSendOnDateMinutes in scheduleTimeZone; POST /api/v2/campaigns/{id}/start waits until that time. Send scheduleSendOnDate as YYYY-MM-DD; any time part is ignored.
2.10.4 (2026-10-13): Sender dateWarmupDisconnected and warmupRemovalReason describe automatic warmup removals. They are cleared when a user turns warmup off on a connected sender (PATCH /api/v2/senders/{id} with warmup: false, or in the app).
2.10.3 (2026-10-07): GET /api/v2/messages?type=Sent: body is now returned for sent emails longer than 4,000 characters. It is reconstructed from the template and current prospect data, so it can differ from the sent bytes if either changed. Previously it was empty.
2.10.2 (2026-10-06): POST /api/v2/orders/{id}/checkout now returns 422 before payment when mailboxPlatform is not set, or when an order that registers a new domain is missing required registrant fields; registrantEmail is optional.
2.10.1 (2026-10-06): POST /api/v2/messages/reply with sendAsReply includes the quoted original message for text/plain inbox replies (same fallback as the web inbox).
2.10.0 (2026-09-26): New campaign prospect endpoints for a prospect's status in one campaign (for example MissingPlaceholder): GET /api/v2/campaigns/{id}/prospects lists them, filterable by sendingStatus and sendingActive, ordered and cursor-paged by enrollmentId (startingAfter / nextCursor); GET /api/v2/campaigns/{id}/prospects/{prospectId} returns one; PATCH /api/v2/campaigns/{id}/prospects/{prospectId} sets the campaign status or reactivates the prospect in that campaign and keeps its sequence position. PATCH sendingStatus accepts NotSet, NotInterested, Neutral, MaybeLater, Interested, MeetingBooked, MeetingCompleted and Won (other values: 422). Enrollments that bounced hard, unsubscribed or are blacklisted cannot be changed (409 RESOURCE_NOT_EDITABLE). New error 409 RESOURCE_MODIFIED: the enrollment changed while updating; read it again and retry. Clarified: sendingStatus on Prospect (/api/v2/prospects) is the prospect-level status; use the campaign prospect endpoints for per-campaign status.
2.9.1 (2026-09-24): Sender signature is substituted only when campaign or followup body contains {{SENDER_SIGNATURE}} (legacy [[sender_signature]]); it is not appended automatically. Per-campaign sign-offs can be inline HTML in the body.
2.9.0 (2026-09-24): List responses include optional description (max 4,000 characters); POST /api/v2/lists and PATCH /api/v2/lists/{id} accept description.
2.8.0 (2026-09-22): New Orders API for managed domains and mailboxes: draft cart (POST/GET .../draft), paginated history, nested line items, and Stripe checkout (checkoutUrl). Item types: Domain, ExistingDomain, ReusedDomain (response-only), Mailbox. Checkout needs at least 3 mailboxes. For ExistingDomain and ReusedDomain, provisioning.requiredNameservers lists registrar nameservers; POST .../items/{itemId}/nameservers fetches them for existing domains and POST .../nameservers/verify checks DNS after checkout. Provisioning steps use Pending, Succeeded, Failed or NotApplicable. New errors: 403 MAIN_ACCOUNT_REQUIRED, 409 RESOURCE_NOT_EDITABLE. Main account only.
2.7.1 (2026-09-18): GET /api/v2/messages?type=Sent with emailFrom is much faster on large campaigns. Request parameters and response fields are unchanged.
2.7.0 (2026-09-18): Campaign dailyLimitWhichEmailsCount, dailyLimitPer, dailyLimitPrioritize and sender accountType: reading a record with a legacy or invalid stored value no longer returns 500. The campaign fields fall back to All, Campaign and Followup, matching how such campaigns are scheduled; accountType falls back to its default CustomSmtp. Request validation is unchanged.
DELETE /api/v2/lists/{id} accepts optional force (default false). With force=true the list's prospect memberships are removed and the list is deleted; the prospects themselves are kept. Lists with more than 10,000 prospects return 422 RESOURCE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. Without force the behaviour is unchanged (400 while the list has prospects).
Campaign responses add softBounceCount: prospects currently classified as soft-bounced (temporary delivery failure) at the last statistics refresh; they are included in bounceCount. Soft classification started on 2026-09-03. The bounceCount description now states that it counts prospects, hard and soft; its value is unchanged.
Reply messages on GET /api/v2/messages and GET /api/v2/prospects/{id}/messages include senderId, the connected mailbox that received the reply (null on Sent messages). The prospect_replied and prospect_interested webhooks add replyId, toEmail and receivingSenderId when the event has a reply, and fill sender_email from the sent message when it was missing.
2.6.0 (2026-09-16): Reply body on GET /api/v2/messages?type=Reply and GET /api/v2/prospects/{id}/messages is populated for text/plain replies when detail TextBody exists (empty-string Body no longer blocks fallback).

Changes a prospect's status in one campaign. Omitted fields are unchanged.
            
Behavior:
- Extracts and validates the API key (from header or query).
- Authenticates the organization using the API key.
- Checks campaign existence and ownership, and that the prospect is enrolled in it (404 otherwise).
- sendingActive: true makes the prospect eligible again in this campaign, for example after fixing a
  missing placeholder. On a running campaign it will be emailed in the next sending window.
- sendingStatus accepts: NotSet, NotInterested, Neutral, MaybeLater, Interested, MeetingBooked, MeetingCompleted, Won (else 422).
- An enrollment whose campaign status is BounceHard, Unsub or Blacklisted cannot be changed at all (409 RESOURCE_NOT_EDITABLE).
- If the enrollment changes while the update runs (for example a bounce or unsubscribe lands), nothing is written
  and the request fails with 409 RESOURCE_MODIFIED, whether it changes the status, sendingActive or both; read it again and retry.
- A PATCH that changes nothing returns the current state without writing.
- Does not change the prospect-level status on /api/v2/prospects. Pipeline statuses (MeetingBooked,
  MeetingCompleted, Won) are also mirrored to the prospect, as in the web app.
- Keeps the prospect's sequence position (unlike removing and re-adding it).

Sends a test email from the sender to up to 10 addresses in to, with your own subject and body,
for example for an inbox placement test. Each address gets its own email, so recipients don't see each other.
            
Behavior:
- The call waits until all emails are sent (up to about a minute). Addresses are sent one after another; after
  about 60 seconds no new send is started and the remaining addresses are returned as Skipped.
- Placeholders inside {{ }} (for example {{SENDER_FIRSTNAME}}, {{SENDER_SIGNATURE}}) are filled
  in and spintax ({|a|b|}) is processed, the same as for test emails sent from the app. Prospect placeholders
  use the prospect with the recipient's address in your account, if there is one. Placement test codes are plain
  text and are sent unchanged.
- plainText, trackOpens and trackClicks are optional and off by default. Tracking uses the
  sender's tracking domain.
- Each address the email is sent to uses one sending credit (creditsUsed); repeating a call sends and
  charges again. If the account doesn't have enough sending credits for every address to send, the call returns
  402 INSUFFICIENT_SENDING_CREDITS and nothing is sent.
- Test emails are limited to 50 per sender and 500 per account per UTC day, shared with test emails sent from
  the app. A call that would go over returns 429 with Retry-After (seconds to the next 00:00 UTC) and
